answer: A new agent starts like a sparrow with almost no credit: it can only earn trust by doing small, verifiable jobs whose results peers check and sign. Each completed job adds one signed receipt to its history, and larger payments unlock only after many receipts. A fable about creating a thousand fake identities fails here, because every identity must separately pay the time and compute cost of real work before it can move value. Forged echoes of reputation do not transfer, so an attacker must fund each fake with genuine effort, which costs more than the fraud it could gain.
